subproblem.title: Pointwise Lipschitz bound by induction over the face dimension (parent step 5 and its Remark)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ. There is c > 0, depending only on P and m, with the following property. Let a ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i. For b ∈ ℤ^P and a finite set J of coordinate indices put F(b, J) := {x : b_i ≤ x_i ≤ b_i + 1 (i ∈ J), x_i = b_i (i ∉ J)} and, for J ≠ ∅, N_{b,J}(x) := max_{k ∈ J} max((x_k − b_k − a_k)/(1 − a_k), (b_k + a_k − x_k)/a_k). Let Ψ_k : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ) be maps with Ψ_{m+1} = id satisfying the recursion: for every j with m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P, every b ∈ ℤ^P, every nonempty J with |J| = j, every x ∈ F(b, J) and every y with y_i = b_i + a_i + (x_i − b_i − a_i)/N_{b,J}(x) (i ∈ J), y_i = x_i (i ∉ J), Ψ_j(x) = Ψ_{j−1}(y). Then for every j with m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P, every b ∈ ℤ^P, every J with |J| = j, every x ∈ F(b, J), and every ρ > 0 such that at most m + 1 indices i ∈ J satisfy |x_i − b_i − a_i| < ρ: (A) Ψ_j(x) ∈ F(b, J); (B) there is a set s of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and Ψ_j(x)_i ∈ ℤ for all i ∈ s; (C) for all y ∈ F(b, J) sufficiently close to x, |Ψ_j(y) − Ψ_j(x)| ≤ (c/ρ)|y − x|. Division by 0 is read as 0 (as in Lean); this only matters at the centre a_F, where N_{b,J} = 0 and the formula gives y = x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ a : Euclid P, (∀ i, |a i - 1 / 2| < 1 / 4) → ∀ Ψ : ℕ → Euclid P → Euclid P, (∀ x, Ψ (m + 1) x = x) → (∀ j, m + 2 ≤ j → j ≤ P → ∀ (b : Fin P → ℤ) (J : Finset (Fin P)) (hJ : J.Nonempty), J.card = j → ∀ x : Euclid P, (∀ i, (i ∈ J → (b i : ℝ) ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ b i + 1) ∧ (i ∉ J → x i = b i)) → ∀ y : Euclid P, (∀ i, y i = if i ∈ J then (b i : ℝ) + a i + (x i - b i - a i) / J.sup' hJ (fun k => max ((x k - b k - a k) / (1 - a k)) ((b k + a k - x k) / a k)) else x i) → Ψ j x = Ψ (j - 1) y) → ∀ j, m + 2 ≤ j → j ≤ P → ∀ (b : Fin P → ℤ) (J : Finset (Fin P)), J.card = j → ∀ x : Euclid P, (∀ i, (i ∈ J → (b i : ℝ) ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ b i + 1) ∧ (i ∉ J → x i = b i)) → ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → (J.filter (fun i => |x i - b i - a i| < ρ)).card ≤ m + 1 → (∀ i, (i ∈ J → (b i : ℝ) ≤ Ψ j x i ∧ Ψ j x i ≤ b i + 1) ∧ (i ∉ J → Ψ j x i = b i)) ∧ (∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, Ψ j x i = z) ∧ ∀ᶠ y in 𝓝[{w : Euclid P | ∀ i, (i ∈ J → (b i : ℝ) ≤ w i ∧ w i ≤ b i + 1) ∧ (i ∉ J → w i = b i)}] x, dist (Ψ j y) (Ψ j x) ≤ c / ρ * dist y x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the supplied proof of the selected parent dimred_mbl_dt_skeleton_retraction [its parent's Lemma D = Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 5.4, with the documented 3/4 → 1/4 erratum] (pointwise bound D̄ψ ≤ c₁/d), in the organization of its closing Remark: induction on the face dimension j inside ℝ^P, one j-face G = F(b, J) at a time, with y₀ := ψ_G(y) = a_G + λ(y − a_G), λ := 1/N_G(y − a_G), the cone K_G of the planes {u : u_i = b_i + a_i (i ∈ J')} (J' ⊆ J, |J'| = n + 1) through the face centre a_G, the scaling dist(y₀, K_G) = λ·dist(y, K_G), and the chain rule. Three formalization adjustments, none of which changes the construction:
(α) The Remark's induction quantity d(y) is replaced by a radius ρ subject to the counting condition C(b, J, u, ρ) below, the coordinate form of 'u is far from K_G' (if C(b, J, u, ρ) fails then n + 1 coordinates in J are within ρ of the centre and dist(u, K_G) < ρ√(n + 1); if dist(u, K_G) < ρ then C(b, J, u, ρ) fails). C scales exactly under y₀ = a_G + λ(x − a_G) (step 3(ii)), which is the Remark's dist(y₀, K_G) = λ·dist(x, K_G). Hence the comparison with the remaining planes of L*(a) (the Remark's 1/4 margin: every other plane of L*(a) is at distance > 1/4 from G) is not needed; by (β), neither is the corrected bound |y₀ − a_G| > 1/4, which the Remark uses for the radial factor. The parent assembly starts the induction on a unit cube with ρ := d(x)/√(m + 2), supplied by the sibling dual_dist_count.
(β) The radial estimate of step 3 is used in the gauge form (1 + 4√j)|y − x|/N(x) of the sibling face_radial, so the factor N(x) = 1/λ cancels exactly in the chain rule (as λ cancels in the Remark).
(γ) D̄ is replaced by a genuine inequality on a relative neighbourhood of x in the face. The Remark's 'points of L_j near y lie in j-faces containing y' and the parent's 'choose δ such that every face meeting B_δ(y₀) contains y₀' become steps 3(iv)–(vi).
Notation. n := m + 1. For b ∈ ℤ^P and a finite index set J:
- F(b, J) := {u : b_i ≤ u_i ≤ b_i + 1 (i ∈ J), u_i = b_i (i ∉ J)}, with centre a_F (coordinates b_i + a_i on J, b_i off J);
- for J ≠ ∅, N_{b,J}(u) := max_{k ∈ J} max((u_k − b_k − a_k)/(1 − a_k), (b_k + a_k − u_k)/a_k) (Finset.sup'; independent of the nonemptiness proof);
- ψ_{b,J} : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is the map (built with WithLp.toLp) with ψ_{b,J}(u)_i = b_i + a_i + (u_i − b_i − a_i)/N_{b,J}(u) for i ∈ J and ψ_{b,J}(u)_i = u_i for i ∉ J; it satisfies the coordinate hypothesis on ψF in face_radial;
- for u ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0, C(b, J, u, ρ) means #{i ∈ J : |u_i − b_i − a_i| < ρ} ≤ m + 1.
REC denotes the recursion hypothesis on Ψ. Applied with y := ψ_{b,J}(u), whose coordinates are exactly the required ones, it gives Ψ_j(u) = Ψ_{j−1}(ψ_{b,J}(u)) whenever m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P, |J| = j and u ∈ F(b, J).
Put K := 1 + 4√P ≥ 1 and c := K^P > 0; c depends only on P (in particular only on P and m).
Claim(j), for m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P: for all b, all J with |J| = j, all x ∈ F(b, J) and all ρ > 0 with C(b, J, x, ρ):
 (A) Ψ_j(x) ∈ F(b, J);
 (B) there is a set s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and Ψ_j(x)_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ s;
 (C) there is δ > 0 with |Ψ_j(y) − Ψ_j(x)| ≤ (K^{j−m−1}/ρ)|y − x| for all y ∈ F(b, J) with |y − x| < δ.
0. Claim(j) for all j ∈ [m + 2, P] gives the theorem with this c. (A) and (B) are its first two conclusions. Because K ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ j − m − 1 ≤ P, K^{j−m−1} ≤ K^P = c, so (C) gives dist(Ψ_j y, Ψ_j x) ≤ (c/ρ)·dist(y, x) for all y ∈ F(b, J) with dist(y, x) < δ, i.e. eventually in 𝓝[F(b, J)] x (Metric.mem_nhdsWithin_iff). If m + 2 > P there is nothing to prove. Claim(j) is proved by induction on j starting at m + 2 (Nat.le_induction), carrying the hypothesis j ≤ P (if j + 1 ≤ P then j ≤ P).
1. Preliminaries. Fix j with m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P, b, J with |J| = j (so J ≠ ∅), F := F(b, J), x ∈ F and ρ > 0 with C(b, J, x, ρ). Write N := N_{b,J} and ψ_F := ψ_{b,J}.
 (a) Since |J| = j ≥ m + 2 > m + 1, some i ∈ J has |x_i − b_i − a_i| ≥ ρ > 0 (otherwise all j indices of J would be counted). In particular x_i ≠ b_i + a_i, so face_radial applies to x, and by its conclusion (1), N(x) ≥ |x_i − b_i − a_i| ≥ ρ.
 (b) If y ∈ F and |y − x| < ρ/2, then C(b, J, y, ρ/2) holds. Indeed, if |y_i − b_i − a_i| < ρ/2, then |x_i − b_i − a_i| ≤ |x_i − y_i| + |y_i − b_i − a_i| < ρ/2 + ρ/2 = ρ, since |x_i − y_i| ≤ |x − y| (PiLp.dist_apply_le). So the set counted for (y, ρ/2) is contained in the set counted for (x, ρ). Applying (a) to y and ρ/2: y_i ≠ b_i + a_i for some i ∈ J.
 (c) By REC, Ψ_j(u) = Ψ_{j−1}(ψ_F(u)) for every u ∈ F.
 (d) By face_radial at x: 0 < N(x) ≤ 1; ψ_F(x) ∈ F; ψ_F(x)_i ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1} for some i ∈ J; and |ψ_F(y) − ψ_F(x)| ≤ (1 + 4√j)/N(x)·|y − x| for every y ∈ F with y_i ≠ b_i + a_i for some i ∈ J, in particular, by (b), for every y ∈ F with |y − x| < ρ/2. For every such y, face_radial at y gives ψ_F(y) ∈ F and ψ_F(y)_i ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1} for some i ∈ J.
2. Base case j = m + 2 (the Remark's case j = n + 1, where L*(a) ∩ G = {a_G}). By (c) and Ψ_{m+1} = id, Ψ_j(u) = ψ_F(u) for every u ∈ F.
 (A) Ψ_j(x) = ψ_F(x) ∈ F by 1(d).
 (B) Take i₀ ∈ J with ψ_F(x)_{i₀} ∈ {b_{i₀}, b_{i₀} + 1} (1(d)) and let s := (all indices ∖ J) ∪ {i₀}. For i ∉ J, ψ_F(x)_i = x_i = b_i ∈ ℤ, and ψ_F(x)_{i₀} ∈ ℤ. Since i₀ ∈ J, |s| = (P − (m + 2)) + 1, so P = m + 1 + |s|.
 (C) Take δ := ρ/2. For y ∈ F with |y − x| < δ, 1(d), N(x) ≥ ρ from 1(a), and m + 2 ≤ P give |Ψ_j(y) − Ψ_j(x)| = |ψ_F(y) − ψ_F(x)| ≤ (1 + 4√(m + 2))/N(x)·|y − x| ≤ (K/ρ)|y − x|, and K = K^{j−m−1}.
3. Inductive step: m + 3 ≤ j ≤ P, and Claim(j − 1) holds. Put y₀ := ψ_F(x) and λ := 1/N(x) > 0. By the formula for ψ_F, y₀_k − b_k − a_k = λ(x_k − b_k − a_k) for k ∈ J (the Remark's y₀ = a_G + λ(y − a_G)) and y₀_k = x_k = b_k for k ∉ J. By (c), Ψ_j(x) = Ψ_{j−1}(y₀).
 (i) Faces through y₀. For i ∈ J and an integer β ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1} put b^{i,β} := b with the i-th entry replaced by β (Function.update), J^i := J ∖ {i} (so |J^i| = j − 1 ≥ m + 2), and G_{i,β} := F(b^{i,β}, J^i). Then G_{i,β} ⊆ F: for u ∈ G_{i,β}, b_k ≤ u_k ≤ b_k + 1 for k ∈ J^i, u_i = β ∈ [b_i, b_i + 1], and u_k = b_k for k ∉ J. If y₀_i = β, then y₀ ∈ G_{i,β}: b_k ≤ y₀_k ≤ b_k + 1 for k ∈ J^i since y₀ ∈ F, y₀_i = β, and y₀_k = b_k for k ∉ J. By 1(d) at least one pair (i, β) with y₀_i = β exists, and there are at most 2j pairs in all.
 (ii) Scaling (the Remark's dist(y₀, K_G) = λ·dist(y, K_G)). If y₀_i = β, then C(b^{i,β}, J^i, y₀, λρ) holds. For k ∈ J^i, b^{i,β}_k = b_k and |y₀_k − b_k − a_k| = λ|x_k − b_k − a_k|, which is < λρ iff |x_k − b_k − a_k| < ρ, since λ > 0. So the counted set is a subset of the one for (b, J, x, ρ), which has at most m + 1 elements.
 (iii) For every pair with y₀_i = β apply Claim(j − 1) to (b^{i,β}, J^i, y₀, λρ). Its (A) gives Ψ_{j−1}(y₀) ∈ G_{i,β} ⊆ F; this is (A) for Ψ_j(x) = Ψ_{j−1}(y₀). Its (B) is (B) for Ψ_j(x). Its (C) gives δ_{i,β} > 0 such that |Ψ_{j−1}(y') − Ψ_{j−1}(y₀)| ≤ (K^{j−m−2}/(λρ))|y' − y₀| = (K^{j−m−2}N(x)/ρ)|y' − y₀| for all y' ∈ G_{i,β} with |y' − y₀| < δ_{i,β}.
 (iv) Nearby boundary points lie on faces through y₀ (parent: every face meeting B_δ(y₀) contains y₀). Choose η > 0 with η ≤ δ_{i,β} for every pair with y₀_i = β and η ≤ |y₀_i − β| for every pair (i ∈ J, β ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1}) with y₀_i ≠ β; for instance the minimum of these finitely many positive numbers and 1.
 (v) Put δ := min(ρ/2, η·N(x)/(1 + 4√j)) > 0. For y ∈ F with |y − x| < δ, 1(d) gives |ψ_F(y) − y₀| ≤ (1 + 4√j)/N(x)·|y − x| < η.
 (vi) Let y ∈ F with |y − x| < δ. By (c), Ψ_j(y) = Ψ_{j−1}(ψ_F(y)). By 1(d) (note |y − x| < ρ/2), ψ_F(y) ∈ F and ψ_F(y)_i = β for some i ∈ J and some β ∈ {b_i, b_i + 1}. If y₀_i ≠ β, then |y₀_i − β| = |y₀_i − ψ_F(y)_i| ≤ |y₀ − ψ_F(y)| < η ≤ |y₀_i − β|, which is impossible; so y₀_i = β and (i, β) is one of the pairs in (iii). Then ψ_F(y) ∈ G_{i,β}: its coordinates k ∈ J^i lie in [b_k, b_k + 1] because ψ_F(y) ∈ F, its i-th coordinate is β, and ψ_F(y)_k = y_k = b_k for k ∉ J. Since |ψ_F(y) − y₀| < η ≤ δ_{i,β}, (iii) and (v) give (the Remark's chain rule)
 |Ψ_j(y) − Ψ_j(x)| = |Ψ_{j−1}(ψ_F(y)) − Ψ_{j−1}(y₀)| ≤ (K^{j−m−2}N(x)/ρ)·|ψ_F(y) − y₀| ≤ (K^{j−m−2}N(x)/ρ)·((1 + 4√j)/N(x))·|y − x| ≤ (K^{j−m−1}/ρ)|y − x|,
 because 1 + 4√j ≤ 1 + 4√P = K. This is (C) of Claim(j) with this δ.
4. By induction Claim(j) holds for all m + 2 ≤ j ≤ P, and step 0 gives the theorem. ∎

proof_key_steps: Counting condition C(x, ρ) gives a coordinate with |x_i − b_i − a_i| ≥ ρ, hence x ≠ a_F and N(x) ≥ ρ, and it passes to y near x with radius ρ/2.
REC plus face_radial: on F, Ψ_j = Ψ_{j−1} ∘ ψ_F, and ψ_F has the radial bound (1 + 4√j)/N(x) near x.
Base case j = m + 2: Ψ_j = ψ_F on F, constant (1 + 4√P)/ρ, plus one extra integer coordinate from the boundary.
Inductive step: y₀ = ψ_F(x) lies on the (j − 1)-faces G_{i,β}; the counting condition scales to radius ρ/N(x) at y₀ (homothety of the cone K_G).
Points ψ_F(y) for y near x lie on faces through y₀; chain the inductive constant K^{j−m−2}N(x)/ρ with (1 + 4√j)/N(x), cancelling N(x).
Constants K^{j−m−1} ≤ (1 + 4√P)^P = c give the uniform bound c/ρ, eventually in 𝓝[F] x.

audit.reason: The type faithfully states the uniform constant, arbitrary family satisfying the recursion, counting hypothesis and three conclusions. The proof establishes noncentrality near x, the base case, exact scaling to ρ/N(x), and finite-face neighbourhood control. The inductive and radial factors cancel, giving the claimed constant. It needs only face_radial: family existence is supplied separately to the parent. Together with counting, cube coverage and the segment lemma, these conclusions prove the exact selected parent.
